newsitem.title: INDIA: India banks need secondary debt trade skills - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India banks need secondary debt trade skills - RBI.

text.p: Indian banks require greater expertise in trading government securities on the secondary market to effectively manage liquidity, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Wednesday.

In its "Report on trend and progress of banking in India, 1995/96 (July-June)," the RBI said the process of cleaning bank balance sheets, one of the objectives of economic reforms started in the early 1990S, could not be complete without increasing the level of securities which are marked to market -- valued at market prices.
At present banks in India are required to value at least 50 percent of their investments in approved securities at market value.
If the market value of the securities is lower than the cost of acquisition, banks are required to create a provision covering the difference.
Over time, banks will have to prepare to mark to market a larger proportion of their approved security portfolio than the present 50 percent, the RBI report said.
"It is therefore essential that banks develop and enhance their treasury management skills," it said.
The RBI noted that this had become particularly important in a deregulated interest rate environment where interest rate risk could become a major factor determining the financial health of a bank.
